brief:
In Gaza, food prices are no longer determined by conventional supply-and-demand dynamics, Shehab Wire reported. Severe shortages have created conditions where merchants exploit hunger to drive up costs, compounding the humanitarian crisis and testing the population's ability to endure.

The reporting indicates that normal market mechanisms have collapsed under the weight of blockade conditions, allowing traders to manipulate pricing in ways that deepen deprivation rather than reflect actual resource availability.
dek: In Gaza, food prices are no longer determined by conventional supply-and-demand dynamics, Shehab Wire reported.
title: Merchants in Gaza weaponize scarcity to inflate prices and erode resistance
